taxonomyNote: NatureServe: the genus Streptopelia sensu lato is weakly supported as monophyletic; species placed in Spilopelia. ADW still files it as Streptopelia chinensis.
fieldMarks: Mourning-dove size but bulkier, rounder tail, no black spots on the wings
Black collar with white spots is the best mark, less obvious on young birds (immatures lack the band)
behavior: Forages on the ground for seeds, in pairs or small groups; comes to feeders
Male display: steep climb with noisy wing-claps, then a gliding circle
habitat: Residential areas, parks and river woods, mostly altered habitats: well-watered suburbs with trees and lawns, farms, stream groves including eucalyptus.
range: Native to Asia; introduced from Asia to Hawaii in the 1800s and to California. NatureServe records it in California, Utah and Hawaii.

lookalikes.name: Mourning dove
lookalikes.howToTell: Spotted dove is bulkier with a rounder tail, has no black wing spots and shows the white-spotted black neck collar.
